sources.concept: HTTPS kuma-dp bootstrap with control-plane CA configuration absent

impact.affected_asset: kuma-dp proxy bootstrap configuration and the data-plane authentication token.
impact.attacker_capability: Intercept the data-plane authentication token and impersonate the control plane to inject a forged bootstrap configuration.
impact.security_effect: Control-plane identity is not authenticated for the affected bootstrap connection, enabling token interception and forged bootstrap delivery by an on-path attacker.

causal_trace.summary: Universal-mode kuma-dp is configured to contact an HTTPS control plane without a supplied control-plane CA certificate.
The bootstrap connection disables TLS peer verification when no CA certificate is configured, rather than retaining system trust validation.
The remote bootstrap HTTP transport sets its TLS configuration to skip verification on the CA-absent path; the data-plane authentication token is then sent over that unverified connection.
An on-path attacker can intercept the authentication token, impersonate the control plane, provide a forged bootstrap configuration, and take over the proxy.

failure.operation: Creation of the remote-bootstrap HTTP transport with TLS peer verification skipped on the no-CA path.

primary_invariant.statement: An HTTPS control-plane bootstrap connection must authenticate the control-plane certificate against configured or system trust unless verification is explicitly opted out for development or testing.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The pre-fix CA-absent branch set TLS verification to be skipped, so lack of an operator-supplied CA silently removed peer authentication.

quality.review_notes: Mechanism and remediation are grounded by the maintainer advisory and inspected fix diff. The bundle contains no issue-specific execution transcript, packet capture, or confirmed test-run result, so reproducibility is not asserted. The OSV record preserves separate legacy github.com/kumahq/kuma and v2 package range events.

remediation.invariant_restored: When a custom CA is not configured, the client leaves TLS verification enabled and can use operating-system trust; certificate skipping is limited to the explicit --skip-verify option.
mitigation_classes: system trust-store certificate validation by default
